# Let's Infer

> Let's Infer turns local AI hardware into one reliable, OpenAI-compatible inference service.

Let's Infer is an open-source, engine-agnostic inference distribution and runtime manager. Start with a model name; it handles hardware matching, exact model artifacts, the engine, lifecycle, safety, telemetry, and updates.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/): Product overview and documentation map.
- [Installation](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/getting-started/installation.html): Install on Linux or macOS and initialize a node.
- [Features](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/features.html): Model installation, serving, replication, observability, safety, and updates.
- [CLI reference](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/reference/cli.html): Stable command-line workflows.
- [Agent skills](https://github.com/letsinferlabs/skills): Portable Let’s Infer workflows for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok Build, DeepSeek Harness, and Hermes Agent.

## Technical concepts

- [Runtime candidates](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/concepts/runtime-packs.html): Exact model, Engine OCI, target, recipe, and evidence bundles.
- [Engine protocol](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/concepts/engine-adapters.html): Engine-agnostic core and adapter boundary.
- [Nodes and replication](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/concepts/sites.html): Main and child nodes, trust, and one stable endpoint.
- [Runtime format](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/reference/runtime-format.html): Runtime schema and publication contract.
- [Develop runtimes](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/contributing/runtimes.html): Runtime and Engine authoring, deterministic validation, and pull-request verification.
- [Watchdog](https://letsinfer.ai/docs/operations/watchdog.html): Telemetry, crash recording, and engine protection.
